  Threat: Threat in Silence: Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen, Alert at Home: I feel on guard even inside my own home, Scanning for Danger: I constantly scan my surroundings for signs of danger
  Memory: Cannot Find Words: I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it, Feels Present Not Past: The memory feels like it is happening right now rather than something that is over, Terror on Recall: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
  Negative Appraisals: Distrust Others: People are not what they seem, Identity Loss: I feel like I don't know myself anymore, Body Unreliable: I can no longer trust my own body

Vignette:
Rohan had always been a man of the sea, spending his days navigating the waters off the coast of Massachusetts as a fisherman. His wife, Leela, would often joke that he was more comfortable on the waves than on dry land. But it was on one fateful day, five years ago, that Rohan's life took a devastating turn. As he was unloading his catch at the dock, a car lost control and careened onto the pier, sending crates of fish flying everywhere. Rohan was pinned beneath the wreckage, his leg crushed beneath a heap of splintered wood. The accident had left Rohan with more than just physical scars. The sound of crunching metal and screams still echoed in his mind, refusing to be silenced. Whenever he tried to recount that day to friends or family, he found himself struggling to find the words, as if the memory was stuck in his throat like a fishbone. Even now, when memories of the accident flooded back, Rohan felt like he was reliving it all over again - the terror, the helplessness, the feeling of being trapped. As time passed, Rohan began to notice changes within himself. He had always been a sociable man, but now the thought of striking up conversations with strangers made his skin crawl. He would catch himself scanning the crowds at the market or the dock, searching for potential threats lurking in every face. Even the silence that once brought him peace now felt oppressive, like a held breath waiting to be released. Rohan couldn't shake off the feeling that danger was always lurking just around the corner, even within his own home. Rohan's widowhood had left him with a deep sense of loss, but it also made him wary of forming new connections. He had come to believe that people were not what they seemed, that behind every friendly smile and warm handshake lay hidden motives and dangers. This distrust seeped into every aspect of his life, making him question even his own body's ability to keep him safe. His leg still ached from the accident, a constant reminder that he was no longer the man he once was. As Rohan went about his daily routine, these fears and doubts swirled around him like a maelstrom. He would find himself constantly on guard, even when he was alone in his small apartment. His friends and family noticed the change in him, but Rohan couldn't explain what was happening - only that he felt lost, adrift in a world that no longer made sense. One day, as he was listening to a news report about a fatal car accident, something inside Rohan snapped. The memories came flooding back, along with the familiar feeling of terror and helplessness. For the first time, Rohan realized that he couldn't keep living like this - always on edge, never at peace. It was then that he made the decision to seek help, hoping that somehow, someway, he could learn to navigate these treacherous waters and find a sense of calm again. As Rohan sat in his therapist's office, his eyes scanning the unfamiliar surroundings with a mix of wariness and desperation, he knew that this was just the beginning of a long and difficult journey. But for the first time in years, he felt a glimmer of hope - a chance to reclaim his life from the darkness that had consumed him, and to find himself once more.
